A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RAG-GESTURE research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and supplementary material are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated appendix content.

before.justification: V1 reports original BEAT2 gesture-generation experiments, quantitative ablations, per-speaker results, and perceptual studies involving 56 participants.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds database-size and prompt-word-count ablations, a reported motion-blending comparison, and runtime measurements.

M1.justification: The body-part VAEs, conditional diffusion model, retrieval algorithms, DDIM latent initialization, and retrieval guidance are retained. Section 10.3 newly documents optional insertion at t=K while explicitly retaining t=T for the current setup; it does not establish a changed implemented procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use BEAT2 for co-speech gesture synthesis, evaluating Scott and all 25 speakers. The added tests vary retrieval databases and prompt settings within this existing coverage. Changing the Table 1 caption from BEAT to BEAT2 corrects its naming.

E2.justification: V2 adds No RAG to the Table 1 comparison and reports a qualitative linear-motion-blending comparator in Section 9.2. Training-based RAG matches the former ReMoDiffuse + Our Retrieval experiment, with expanded implementation documentation; the principal external baselines remain.

E3.justification: New protocols hold the single-speaker model fixed while varying retrieval-database coverage and test maximum prompt word counts of one, two, and three. Existing splits, metrics, training settings, and participant counts remain. The change from three to four user studies corrects wording: both appendices already describe four.

E4.justification: V2 adds focused diagnostics of single-speaker training versus retrieval-database size (Table 6), prompt-word-count sensitivity (Table 7), and interpolation artifacts from motion blending (Section 9.2). Existing retrieval-strategy and insertion-strength ablations remain; the per-speaker analysis is relocated rather than added.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same user-study significance markers using p<0.05. V2 adds no repeated-run counts, random-seed information, confidence intervals, or other uncertainty-reporting procedures.

E6.justification: Table 1 changes discourse Beat Alignment from 0.417 to 0.471, matching Tables 2–3. Table 3 changes latent-initialization-only L1 divergence from 9.228 to 9.29, which is not equivalent rounding. V2 also adds No RAG entries, database-size and prompt ablation results, runtime measurements, and reported blending artifacts. Existing baseline scores and user-study preference percentages otherwise remain stable.

T1.justification: Section 3.3 corrects the no-guidance example's starting state from z_retr^(0), t=0 to z_retr^(T), t=T. This resolves a mathematical inconsistency about where the initial retrieval constraint applies. Equations (1)–(6) and their underlying derivation remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: semantic gesture generation through explicit retrieval, inference-time latent initialization and guidance, controllable retrieval influence, and improved perceptual quality. The additional evidence does not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: V2 interprets the single-speaker ablation as evidence of data-limited underfitting and attributes the small database-size benefit to better matching. It adds explanations of interpolation artifacts and prompt-setting flexibility. Existing limitations concerning sparse exemplars and incorrect retrievals are retained and moved.

D1.justification: V2 identifies discopy for discourse parsing, documents optional insertion timing, and specifies SemanticGesticulator's merging strategy within the existing training-based comparator. Section 10.6 newly reports retrieval times of 0.03 seconds and 1.52 seconds, plus 26.93-second diffusion inference on an RTX3090 with batch size 32. Most architecture, optimizer, and prompting details were already present.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations to discopy and LivelySpeaker, removes SEEG, and expands distinctions from SemanticGesticulator concerning inference-time operation, prosody, and retrieval flexibility. BERT and COMO publication updates refer to existing cited works rather than new research coverage.

P1.justification: V2 repairs the broken introductory gesture-classification sentence, clarifies inpainting and baseline descriptions, corrects the single-speaker FID description from lower to higher, and fixes the user-study count. Supplementary sections are reordered and expanded, while the main narrative structure remains.

P2.justification: V2 adds Tables 6–7, expands Table 1 with a No RAG row, and revises labels and formatting in Figure 6 and Table 2. Appendix content is rearranged and captions receive small clarifications. The principal method diagrams and perceptual-result plots retain their structure.

improvement.justification: Targeted controls in Tables 6–7, corrected numerical and descriptive inconsistencies, and clearer implementation and runtime documentation improve interpretability and reproducibility. The gains are limited: the main empirical foundation remains unchanged, the underfitting explanation is indirect, and testing one to three prompt words does not establish the claimed flexibility for any configuration.
